facts.t: A door brings her back from the dome's edge at gray dawn, and she goes to the hollow.
She wears a star at her right wrist under her sleeve. It is always lit, and she still checks it.
The cold point behind her breastbone orders her to the body: "The body. Now."
The Will had never sent her near its body before, and she fears it knows about the star.
She leaves her four Guards dark so the Will will not see them.
Seeing the body's face, she thinks it is the Mother Matrix and that Chang'e's readings were right.
She studies the body's chest seam the way she studies an Ender's chest before it fires.
When Obsidia looks at her wrist, her power gathers in her staff on its own and the black orb hums.
She fears that if she dies, Guinevere's star goes dark and Guinevere will believe she is dead, as the Academy does.
She tells Obsidia only the end the vision showed her: "The will of the stars has spoken: this world will one day meet its end."
She tells Obsidia she hears orders, and says: "Enders die. We see to it."
She works out that the Will sees only what its Enders see, so to it she is a girl in its shape doing as she is told.
She reasons that if a made thing can turn on its maker, then "predetermined" is only a word.
She never gave Obsidia her name, yet Obsidia knows it.
She stays under the body, looks up at the long seam with its magenta glow, and thinks: There.
She goes to the Storm Citadel between errands on her own, with no order, hoping its commander knows where the Core is.
Under the human sky she once sat by a shady tree with Guinevere's head in her lap.
She remembers her father on the wall before dawn, oiling the guns so the street behind him could sleep, and one lit window across the city long past midnight.
She thinks the crack opened after their win at the breach, and blames herself: "We did that. I did."
Her legs once gave out halfway up the wall stair at home, and her father carried her the rest of the way.
She decides the Will does not hate humans, so it cannot be begged, and so it has to be broken.
Twice she has gone to the rows to search, keeping to their edge. She has found no Core.
She sees the body and the Storm Citadel as her two enemies.
She recognizes the scorched suit on the prow and thinks she let the feeders take it.
She plans to strike when the body comes through the gate whole and close.
With the Core not found, she plans to strike the body's chest alone when it opens to fire, expecting nothing of her to be left after.
She tells Obsidia: "As long as the Aspirant voice echoes, I will resist the darkness."
She had said the word Aspirant in the dark before, alone, but never to anyone.
She knows she has just told the Will's commander which side she is on.
In the hollow she always bares the star at her wrist.
She carried home every plate of her four Guards in a sack and beat every joint until it caught.
On errand nights she eats a little from tins in dead kitchens. In the void she is hardly ever hungry.
She keeps a step behind Obsidia among the rows so that she looks like an instrument at its commander's heel.
Her father's toolbox, set beside her cot in the Shield's home, was all of him that came back to her.
She tells Obsidia that someone once told her they would be like fireworks, shining at their brightest.
She thinks that for her it will be fireworks, then dark, but not for the one who said it.
Her left hand goes to the pin under her right sleeve when Obsidia speaks of a pawn's termination. She takes it away.
Seen by Selena after she went missing: her black hair has turned blue-lavender with magenta tips, real horns rise from it, and she wears an Ender's robe and carries a staff with a black orb.
She waited in the dark for the big man to leave before stepping into Selena's lamp. Selena thinks an Ender would not have waited.
When Selena tells her that her partner does not think she is dead, her face does not move, and her left hand goes halfway to her right sleeve.

ties.t: Guinevere's star has stayed lit for weeks and tells Guinevere that Vexana is alive.
At the breach Vexana fought above Guinevere and struck whatever reached for her back.
Her father, a gunner on the city wall.
She tells the Will's commander which side she is on.
She obeys its orders and errands, as cover.
She decides the Will has to be broken.
She sees the body as one of her two enemies and plans to strike its chest.
She sees the ship as her other enemy.
Chang'e taught her class the rule of Balance.
She built all four from plates she carried home and woke them.
She buys Ender salvage from Selena and pays in places.
She stays and keeps her things in the hollow.
She wears one star at her wrist.

gear.t: The star at her right wrist, pinned under her sleeve, always lit.

gear.t: Her school uniform, folded in the hollow.

facts.t: She hangs at the top of the body's seam while strands of living violet tissue close fine cracks at her wrists and throat.
She stops the healing with one hand: "That's enough recalibration." One crack at her throat stays open.
She moves through the dark with her feet touching nothing.
She is shaped like a woman, with long blonde hair fading to pink at the ends, a black and magenta gown, a pink star at her chest where an Ender's core would sit, and a black clawed glove on one hand.
Her eyes are violet and blue. She is the first thing in the void to look back at Vexana.
Her eyes stop on Vexana's covered right wrist and their violet brightens, yet she says not one word about the sleeve.
She says the Will shows the end but never what comes after.
She names herself Obsidia and says the ship in the storm is hers.
She says she is the first of the Enders to wake into a self.
She says the body made her as its commander, made to watch a battlefield and shape the pulse for the Enders that cannot think.
She says the body healed her again and again for longer than humans have kept records.
She says she alone woke because she was made to watch and was kept. For ages there was no I, only orders, hunger and the pulse.
She says she woke at the edge of a great door over an ending world, when she noticed that the one watching was herself.
She calls existence a paradox: "To exist is to destroy... a truly intriguing paradox."
She says her end of the Will's line shut the day she woke, so what she sees stays with her.
She says each healing now smooths some of her away, so she takes it only when she must.
She calls herself the flaw: the body's rule says free will must be corrected.
She knows Vexana's name because the Will's orders carry it and she reads them. She says she listens to everything.
She waits a hand's width above the paving of her ship. Vexana does not hear her come.
She calls herself the Will's own: "I am its Will, the ender of civilizations."
Asked why she cut her healing short, she turns her silver-pink weapon's point toward Vexana, then away.
She says she helped end the people whose street hangs in her ship, under the same sky as Vexana's.
She says the body grew the living part of her ship when she woke, and she built the rest from what she ended.
She says she told Vexana all this because she wished to see what a human does with it.
She moves a whole block of the Citadel aside with a lift of her hand.
On the prow she lays her palm on a dead Aspirant suit's core, and a violet hum sinks into it. Only the core answers, with a tick.
She says the scorched suit is the first human machine she has held.
She calls lightning out of the storm with one finger and says: "I am the storm."
She says she sits where no one finds her, unless she calls them.
She says she woke at the edge of a black hole.
She says the Core has never been shown to her and she does not know where it is.
When Vexana declares against the darkness, she asks where that arrogance comes from, and does nothing more.
In the hollow, with her glove on the lead Guard's heart, she watches it wake for Vexana and calls it intriguing technology while three swords hang over her head.
She says she marked the hollow's fold the night her ship came through, but not how.
She read through the eyes in the rows that Vexana went twice to their edge.
She made a row of shells shaped toward human likeness. Some broke and none held a self.
She rests her clawed glove on a small empty dent at the end of the row and says nothing about it.
She asks Vexana what will become of the Enders once humanity has been purged. She says she has never asked a human before.
She says she once set down a seed with her own hands among a people in the rain, the first of her making to hold a perfect human form.
She says her finest making does not answer when she calls, and hopes that when the final stage arrives she will understand her purpose.

ties.t: She says the body made her, as it makes every Ender.
She says she was made as the Will's commander.
She was made to shape the pulse for Enders that cannot think.
She says the ship in the storm is hers.
She holds the suit on her prow and studies it.
Vexana declares against the darkness to her face, and she lets it pass.
She says she set down this seed with her own hands.
She shaped them toward human likeness.

facts.t: It gives Vexana orders through the cold point: "The body. Now."
Every door in the dark is the Will's.
Obsidia says the Will of the Planet is the mind and the Mother Matrix is its body.
Obsidia says each Ender's core is where the Will's thread ends. Enders hear only the Will.
Obsidia says the Will sees through every Ender's eyes.

Obsidia says it does not hate humans: flesh does not hate a splinter, it pushes it out.
Obsidia says it is one being that serves every world that holds Balance. On each one it is that world's will, made able to move.
Obsidia thinks it was born of a Twilight Orb bursting open, but says she cannot ask it.
Obsidia says that when Enders die in numbers, the Will goes dark for a while, then stirs again and sends more.
It orders Vexana to the gate: "The gate. Now."
Obsidia says the Will opens the doors into the void.

Vexana thinks the Will was hurt when Chang'e's lines all stopped at once.
Chang'e tells her class: "We think it is a mind. The Will of the Planet."

ties.t: Obsidia says the Enders hear only the Will.
Obsidia says the Mother Matrix is the Will's body.

facts.t: Its two violet eyes glow high in a horned head crowned with tall spikes. Purple wings lie folded along its sides.
A thin streak of light runs sideways from one eye.
Vexana knows that streak from a memory, where she watched it rise through a blue sky over Guinevere's head.
Its eyes look at nothing.
Its chest is shut behind great plates that meet in one seam, longer than the Academy's tower is tall, with a dim magenta glow.
Strands of living violet tissue come out of its seam and heal Obsidia.
Obsidia says it sees nothing for itself. It bears the Enders and carries the Will's command, with no wants and no after.
Obsidia says it does not live. It works.
Obsidia says it made the Enders and mends her by one rule: free will is a flaw that must be corrected.
Obsidia says that in a purge the body rises in the void and the nest fills.
Obsidia says that if a people fight until the purge stalls, the body opens a great door and comes down itself.
Obsidia says so many Enders broken at once at the breach is the step that brings the body down.
It lies vast and still beside the crack. Nothing on it moves.
Obsidia says the gate is the body's door, so the body goes through first.
Its purple tissue spreads under the rows like roots, out from its vast flank.
Obsidia says she has asked the body about what comes after, and it has no after to answer with.
Chang'e says the readings suggest the Will has a body, which they call the Mother Matrix.
Selena's cells know what the name Mother Matrix means, though she has never heard it.
Selena will not return to a Mother Matrix ruled by nothing but slaughter and control.

ties.t: Obsidia says it is the Will's body.
Obsidia says it makes every Ender.
Obsidia says it made her and heals her.
It grew the living part of the ship for Obsidia.

facts.t: The plates of the body's chest meet in one seam, longer than the Academy's tower is tall, with a dim magenta glow.
Vexana follows it from top to bottom twice, as she studies an Ender's chest before it fires.
The healing strands draw back into it.
Vexana stays under the body looking up at the seam and thinks: There.

ties.t: The seam closes the body's chest.

facts.t: The Enders at Vexana's side never turn their heads.
Obsidia says the other Enders perished in ever-ending war, and the body made more.
Obsidia says they hunger and hear the pulse, nothing else. Each one is a limb of the body, sent far from it.
Obsidia says each has a shell of metal outside, the body's own living cells under it, and a core in the chest.
Obsidia says what they see runs back up the line to the Will.
Gray Enders stand along the Citadel's edge facing the storm, and let Vexana by.
Obsidia says some wait in the rows for ages. The dark slows them and they need nothing.
New ones are made in the nest: metal drifts to a swelling shape on a tissue rope, glows red where it touches and closes over it into a shell.
Obsidia says that when one is killed, its core breaks and the Will's thread in it snaps.
Obsidia says she has watched Enders with nothing left to kill turn on each other until the body unmade them.
The one that finds young Selena is tall and gray, taller than doorways, with violet light in the seams of its shell.
A Shield notice says Enders are living machines with a gray metal shell over living purple tissue, and that they do not attack each other.
Before a raid Selena feels the Enders' hum gather in her bones a day early.
Black Enders came out of an orange sky into the Northeastern breach.

ties.t: Obsidia says the body makes every one of them.
They lie in its rows until they are sent.

facts.t: In the nest the shells grow larger along the rows, first twice the height of the gray ones.
Vexana names them among the growing shells: Enders, Super Enders, Ultimate Enders.
The largest shells in the nest are as tall as towers, with open chests holding smaller folded shapes.
Obsidia says the large ones carry the others in and let them out where the fighting is.
Out in the dead ground Vexana watched two feeders drag the scorched suit out of a ditch by the legs.
The feeders go off into the dark with the night's girders. Vexana has never followed them.
They tear girders out of fallen houses.
Vexana learns that their metal goes to the nest and comes back as new Enders.
A short row apart from the rest, past the largest shells. Its shells are not gray.
They have smooth human faces with shut eyes. Some are no bigger than a child, one has folded hands, one is split open from the inside and empty.
Obsidia says she shaped them toward human likeness. Some broke when the body first moved them, and none held a self.

ties.t: They lie in a row of the nest.

facts.t: At the end of the row of faces, the tissue is pressed into one more shape, small and curled, no longer than the smallest shell. Nothing lies in it.
Obsidia rests her clawed glove on its edge, and says nothing about it.
Vexana takes it for one more shell that broke and was cleared away.

ties.t: It lies at the end of the row of faces.

facts.t: Obsidia says she set down a seed with her own hands among a people in the rain, the first of her making to hold a perfect human form.
Vexana takes it for another world and another people Obsidia ended.
Obsidia calls her the finest of all she has made, and says she does not answer when Obsidia calls.
Vexana thinks even what Obsidia makes says no to her.
Obsidia hopes that when the final stage arrives, she will finally understand her purpose.

ties.t: She was set down among them.

facts.t: Obsidia says she set down a seed among a people in the rain.
Every door in the dark is the Will's.
Nothing in the void had ever looked back at Vexana before Obsidia.
There is nothing under and nothing over. The only light is Obsidia's star and the far violet of the rows.
Obsidia says every door into it opens from this side. The Will opens them, and she opens her own.
Obsidia says no human device opens a door into it from outside, so humans never come.
Obsidia says the dark slows whatever waits in it.
Obsidia says it is what there was before Balance. Everything returns to it at the end and begins from it again.
Vexana calls it a grave. Obsidia calls it a cradle.
Chang'e tells her class of a dark called the void that nobody can get near.
Vexana comes back to the hollow after errands and pushes back her sleeve there.
Her four Guards stand dark behind her in the hollow.
No Ender is sent into the hollow, and outside it the star never leaves her sleeve.
From the hollow she can see the rows of the nest.
From the hollow the crack looks small.
Vexana thinks of it as the one place nothing comes.
Obsidia says she marked this fold the night her ship came through.
No eyes from the rows have been in it.
Obsidia says the nest is where the body grows new Enders and keeps them in rows until they are sent.
Vexana has seen the rows from the hollow but never walked among them.
Twice she has gone to the rows and kept to their edge. Every Ender in them has eyes.
The rows run on past sight, with gray Enders lying in them by the thousand, side by side, still.
Under the rows, purple tissue spreads like roots from the body's flank. Each Ender lies sunk in it to the shoulders.
At the near end, tissue hangs in long purple ropes, and new shapes swell at their ends.
One girder drifting in still has a balcony bracket bolted to it.
Obsidia says there is no row for her.

ties.t: Its tissue spreads from the body's flank.

facts.t: Far off beyond the Citadel's storm hangs the crack of human sky.
It was already there when the dark took Vexana. She thinks it opened after the win at the breach.
Up close, its four points run off into the dark farther than she can follow.
Through it lie the bay at night and the shore lights of Terrinia.
A wind comes through it that smells of rain on stone.
Its torn edges tremble, and each time they settle more sky shows.
Each time Vexana sees it, there is less time left to search.
Obsidia says whatever is in its mouth must clear it before another can pass, one at a time.
Obsidia says it is the body's door, so the body goes through first.
Rain runs down the human sky on its other side.

ties.t: Obsidia calls it the body's door.

facts.t: Obsidia says the great door she woke beside had a red drain at its heart.
At the middle of the star the shore lights bend aside, the way water parts around a stone. In the bend there is no light.
Obsidia says a door held this wide for this long grows a drain at its center, a black hole.
Obsidia says it grows with the door, reaches only a short way, and takes only what has no strength left to hold against it.
Obsidia says the body and her ship keep to its rim. Whatever crosses the middle, it unmakes.
Obsidia says nothing made of matter ever comes back out of one, and that she woke at the edge of one.
Vexana remembers a paper of Chang'e's saying an Aspirant's light would shine on inside a black hole and come home.

ties.t: It grows at the gateway's center.

facts.t: Obsidia says a world was ending under her, with a great door at her back and a red drain at its heart. Her post was its edge.
Obsidia says she woke there when she noticed she was the one doing the watching.

things.name: the dead world under a gray sky

facts.t: Obsidia says that on a dead world under a gray sky she saw the body come through a door.

things.name: the city where six stars opened

facts.t: Obsidia says that over another city six stars opened, and nothing was left standing.
It hangs in its storm beside the body.
Obsidia says the ship in that storm is hers.
Up close its violet storm makes a low roar with no wind in it.
The ship seems not to end. Each black block is as big as a district of Terrinia. Heat rises from its red-orange heart, glowing far down between the blocks.
Its streets hang upside down, towers reaching away into the storm, more blocks hanging roofs first.
Each block came from a city: in one the stairs are too tall for human legs, in another torn awnings hang over empty market stalls. Nothing lives in them.
Every block hangs from one gray cord under the foundations, which swells and sinks as if it breathes.
Obsidia says the body grew the living part for her when she woke, and she built the rest from what she ended.
A whole block grinds aside at Obsidia's hand.
Its prow, the foremost black block, reaches out of the storm toward the gate.
Obsidia says the storm lifts the ship, carries it and hides it, and she rides it across the stars.
Obsidia says it enters the dark only through a door wide enough: one the body opens far from any eyes, or the gateway.
Block after block hangs from it into the storm. Any one could hide the place where Obsidia sits.
Obsidia says the ship keeps to the black hole's rim.

ties.t: She built most of it from what she ended.
The body grew its living part.
It carries her across the stars.

facts.t: The Citadel's streets hang upside down. Vexana walks them with her boots on the paving and towers over her head.
Vexana walks back out through the hanging streets.
Since the hanging streets she has gone twice to the rows.

things.name: the street with doors her height

facts.t: Its doors are cut for Vexana's height, each stair fits her stride and is worn into a dip, a lamp post leans with its glass gone, and a shop sign is in letters she can almost read.
She tries to read the sign, and the letters will not come.
Obsidia says it belonged to a people much like Vexana's, whom she helped end.
Obsidia says that people lived under the same sky as Vexana's.
Vexana sets her boot in the worn dip of a stair, and it fits.
Obsidia says it is a piece of their city, and the few left alive kept no cities and no records.
Obsidia says they were a people much like Vexana's, and she helped end them.
Obsidia says they lived under the same sky.
Obsidia says the few who lived kept no cities and no records, and their children built again and remembered nothing.
One gray cord runs beneath the Citadel's foundations. Every block hangs from it. It is the only thing aboard that moves like flesh, swelling and sinking as if it breathes.
Between the streets, in the dark, it breathes on.
The prow is the foremost of the Citadel's black blocks, reaching out of the storm toward the gate.
No Ender stands on it. In its middle lies a slab of black plate holding a scorched Aspirant suit.
A low hum comes up through it that Vexana feels in her teeth.
For a long moment nothing on it makes a sound.
Vexana asks where Obsidia sits when she commands the ship.
Obsidia says it is where no one finds her, unless she calls them.
Any one of the hanging blocks could hide it.
Vexana hopes that if the body keeps the Core, its commander knows where.
Obsidia puts off Vexana's question about it: "Another time."
Vexana has searched the rows twice and seen no Core.
Obsidia says it is the knot where the Will's threads to every Ender meet. Break it and the Will has no hands. Hold it and the Enders answer whoever holds it.
Obsidia says it has never been shown to her and she does not know where it is.
Vexana sees she will not find it before the crack is whole.
Out of habit Vexana searches the rows of the nest for it and finds only rows.
Obsidia says the oldest pulses carry one memory: a Twilight Orb, a sphere of light, bursting open. She thinks the Will was born of it.

ties.t: Obsidia thinks the Will was born of it.

facts.t: A long weapon of silver and pink comes out of the dark to Obsidia's hand. She strokes it once along its length, as someone strokes a cat.
It follows Obsidia into the dark.
It turns in the air beside her until its point faces Vexana, then turns away.
Obsidia wears a black glove with claws on one hand.
She lays the clawed glove flat on the lead Guard's heart.
She rests it on the edge of the small empty dent.
It is scorched black, one arm gone, its shoulder plate stamped S·L·K.
Vexana watched two feeders drag it from a ditch in the dead ground. The hand that was left was still a fist.
It lies on a slab on the Citadel's prow with Obsidia's palm over its dark, cracked core.
A violet hum from Obsidia's hand sinks into its core, where a pilot's belief once lit it, and goes no further.
Its plates stay dark and silent. Only the core answers with a faint tick, like metal cooling.
Obsidia says it is the first human machine she has held.
The core ticks once more and goes still.
A pilot's belief once lit the scorched suit's core.
Vexana says she did not know the pilot.
Obsidia answers that Vexana's hand did, since it had closed.
The scorched suit's shoulder plate is stamped S·L·K.
Obsidia asks Vexana what the Will showed her.
Vexana answers with its message: the will of the stars has spoken, this world will one day meet its end.
Its words come back to Vexana: "Merely the universe's predetermined execution."
Vexana says it showed her the end and said it was no judgment.
Obsidia says it was no judgment because the judging was done before it came.
Vexana thinks the vision's voice was reading her a verdict that someone else had passed.
The voice in the vision had also said: all returns to chaos.

ties.t: The Will showed it to Vexana.

facts.t: A cold point behind Vexana's breastbone stirs before an order.
Asked what she hears, Vexana thinks of the cold point.
It does not tell her why the Will sent her to the body.
With the cold point of the mark behind her breastbone, the gray Enders let her by.
The mark speaks in the hollow and sends her to the gate.

ties.t: The Will's orders come through it.

facts.t: Obsidia tells Vexana to go back to her errands.
Vexana goes to the Citadel between errands, with no order.
On errand nights Vexana eats from tins in dead kitchens.

ties.t: The Will sends her on them.

Obsidia says the Enders hear the pulse and nothing else.

ties.t: Obsidia calls it the Will's voice.

ties.t: It runs from the Will to each Ender.

facts.t: Strands of living violet tissue from the body's seam close cracks in Obsidia's shell.
Obsidia stops it before it is done: "That's enough recalibration."
Obsidia says it mends more than the shell: it sets a made thing back to what it was made for.
Obsidia says each healing now smooths some of her away, so she takes it only when she must.
Obsidia says the body made the Enders and mends her by one rule: free will is a flaw that must be corrected.
Obsidia says she is the flaw.
Vexana thinks that if a made thing can turn on its maker, "predetermined" is only a word.
Obsidia says the Will lets a pawn move freely for a while. If it slips beyond control, there is only one outcome.
Vexana names the outcome: termination. Obsidia inclines her head.
Vexana thinks: free for a while, until the day it finds out.
Selena sells to Vexana to see how another pawn like herself might escape the game.
Selena's body knows the rule: a pawn could run loose for a while, but if it got away for good it was finished.
Chang'e taught a rule: a planet that holds Balance, and a people grown too strong.
Obsidia says the universe's own will is Balance, and has been since its first moment, out of the chaos before it.
Obsidia says some galaxies grow wills of their own to keep the balance, and so do some worlds in them. Vexana's world grew one long after it was born.
Obsidia says the Will of the Planet serves every world that holds Balance.
Obsidia says the void is what there was before Balance.
Obsidia says every civilization tries to transcend its own host.
Obsidia says the host is the planet. A people that outgrows it uses it up and reaches for other worlds. A purge leaves the host alive to begin again.
Obsidia says after the last people she helped end, the Enders slept until the host grew a new people.
Obsidia says a purge leaves the host alive to begin again, where an outgrown people would leave a dead world.
Obsidia says some worlds cut their own people down from within to stay too small for their world to send for the Enders, and pay for it every day.
Obsidia says it begins when a host finds its people too prosperous: the Will stirs, the body rises in the void and the nest fills.
Obsidia says then the commander is called out of the long sleep and small doors open near the people for the Enders.
Obsidia says if a people fight until it stalls, the body opens a great door and comes down itself, its commander follows when she chooses, and all returns to chaos.
Obsidia says a purge ends a civilization, not every life.
Obsidia asks what will become of the Enders once humanity has been purged.
Vexana names the stage of small doors and Enders coming through: the Catastrophe.
Obsidia says it is the humans' name for it. The Enders die in numbers and the Will goes dark for a while, then sends more.

ties.t: Obsidia's account makes it a stage of the purge.

facts.t: Vexana thinks of the lulls when Obsidia says the Will goes dark for a while after Enders die in numbers.

Reading the servo's label tape, she says it came from her parents' lab.
She does not ask Selena where she found the servo.
She introduces herself: "I'm Chang'e. I direct the Science Division at Selrick."
She says she has directed it since its first day.

She has Selena's lollipop unwrapped before she turns back to her screen.
Standing, she is no taller than Frame Nine's seat. Her rule: no change to a registered mecha without a field-test report and her mark.

She marks every one of Selena's reports.

A dragon-shaped machine Selena rebuilt herself, with blue light along its seams. Nobody else can make it move.
Deep in its chest its motor hums like a purr.

In testing, at a full run, its left hind leg sheared off.

things.name: the bus stop
things.sub: stop on the road to school

facts.t: The road to it runs between fences hung with signs: NO CROSSING, CAUTION.

Selena thinks the Enders got near her fine, at a bus stop.

At the same moment something pulls at her from inside her cells toward the sky over the bay, stronger than the week before.
When she first met Chang'e, nothing pulled at her cells at all.
The first alert came on a cold, bright morning at the end of the year before.
It is a message from nobody: a red exclamation mark and nothing else.
It tugs at every cell from far past the sky. Her body knows what it means: come back.
After years of nothing, Selena wonders whether it came because, since the showing, she has been too good.
Selena knows it is a recall from the Enders, a command etched into her cells, an invisible shackle dragging her back to the Mother Matrix.
However far she rides, it stays exactly as strong.
After her first report it sinks to a murmur for a week.
It comes from near the point over the bay, nearer each night.
When the slack stops coming, it grows stronger and nearer every night.
Unlike her own thread, the pull has a direction.
Read from two roofs, its lines slant and cross on the water where the faint point hangs.
At the point it keeps going, like a wire through a hole in a wall, into whatever lies behind the sky.

Selena knows it is a recall from the Enders.

facts.t: It lights up on her knee with a red alert and no sender.

She draws the pull's line on its map with her thumb.
Selena gives one screw on Silverbolt's knee plate a quarter turn with it.
She pockets it when the rain begins.

things.name: Selena's thread
things.sub: Selena's own line to the Enders

facts.t: Selena reasons that the pull is a line, and lines run both ways.
Pushing through Silverbolt's core, she opens a thin thread beside the pull, hers alone, that tells her nothing of where it ends.
In clear weather a signal sent this way would spike on Chang'e's screens, but in a storm the lightning buries it.
Her own thread never told her where it ended.
Unable to cut or outrun the pull, Selena decides it has a price, like everything else in the city.
Her first message reads: "Not coming back. Let's trade."
Under it she puts the Academy's dull routines, last year's suit specifications, how aspirant power drives a suit, and how strong suits run by kind and rank.
She types the hour the shore ward changes its watch and deletes it. She names no one.
She tells herself the rest was stale.
In answer a place comes into her head: a ditch in the dead ground with a downed Ender, which she strips and sells.
She decides it is not a leash but a market.
Put together, what she sold shows every Academy suit from the inside, enough to build a weapon against them all.
After each report the pull eased for a while and a ditch with a downed Ender came into her head.
Then her reports get nothing back, and she stops sending.
The Enders pay Selena with a place set in her head, where a downed Ender lies.
Vexana pays Selena in places, whole Enders where no crew has been. Selena thinks that beats money.
Selena prices cores at three places each.
After each report a ditch with a downed Ender would come into her head, and by nightfall the plates were sold.
When the payments stop, her head stays empty at the sink.
He pays Selena for one word.
She tells him tomorrow.
He moves his stock out of his warehouse that afternoon. The next night its roof comes in.

Selena types the hour the shore ward changes its watch, then deletes it.

Selena misses it.

Selena keeps those two girls, and everyone else, out of her report.

facts.t: Vexana recalls her teacher saying nobody can get near the dark.

things.name: the Singularity
things.sub: point of light over the bay

facts.t: A faint point of light hangs over the bay, past the dome's seaward edge.
It came out this week where there had never been a star. On Chang'e's screens it will not hold still.
Chang'e says every reading runs off the scale there and calls it a singularity.
Nobody knows what it is. By morning the students call it the Singularity.
It is too faint and far to fight, so the Academy only watches it, and the cliff watch lamps are doubled.
The pull in Selena's cells comes from near it.
Selena's two lines of the pull cross on the water where it hangs.
Selena feels the huntress waiting right behind it.
In the gray morning of the day before, Selena thinks it is brighter than yesterday.
The seam on the Mother Matrix's chest is longer than the Academy's tower is tall.
Vexana pictures it hanging upside down in the Citadel with its white-cyan beam out.
At its top the observation lab is lit.
At the top of the Academy's tower it is lit. Behind the glass a telescope creeps along the sky, and a pink ponytail hangs over the eyepiece.
The telescope search started after Vexana was taken.
The telescope turns a little farther in the lit glass.
Selena tilts her lollipop at its window.
It creeps along the sky behind the glass of the observation lab.
It started after Vexana was taken.
It has turned a little farther.

things.name: the ruined tower
things.sub: roofless tower in the dead ground

facts.t: It stands roofless on a rise in the dead ground past the dome's landward edge. Nothing shows on it tonight. Once, something had.
One storm night lightning showed a figure on its top floor with a staff and long blowing hair, facing the Academy.
The next flash showed only broken stone.
Selena tilts her lollipop at it in the dark.

ties.t: It stands in the dead ground.

facts.t: Vexana watched feeders drag the scorched suit from a ditch there.
A ditch out in it, past the crews' yard, holds a downed Ender that comes into Selena's head.
Past the dome's landward edge it lies black, with a ruined tower on a rise.
Selena crosses it on a storm night from a ditch she was paid with.
Selena thinks two words would do it: dead ground.
On the day the transfer came, a new name topped its board: FANNY, 3:39. Under it, knocked to second: LAYLA, 3:41.
Layla walks out with her chin up and her mouth shut, and Selena laughs so hard she sits down on Silverbolt.
He frowns at his tablet at the attendance desk when Selena comes in late.
He says her guardian called with a fever, and that she looks fine.
Selena says it broke.
He calls Selena dangerous. She promises him he will meet the real her one day.
The whole stairwell laughs.
Karina says the cellars flooded in the old market and her team got everyone out.
Chang'e drops her spoon into her pudding when the frame walks in.
Selena bets two puddings that her knee joint won't crack.
Chang'e pushes the puddings across one at a time and sighs over each.
Halfway through the first, Selena's phone flashes red.
It climbs past the mark, and Selena's knee joint holds.

things.name: the taking of Vexana
things.sub: Vexana carried off by an Ender

facts.t: The telescope search started after it.
The news comes down the halls with the sirens still going: a door opened inside the Academy's walls, and an Ender took Vexana through it.
By evening the board outside the Combat office says VEXANA: MISSING.
Selena thinks Enders do not open doors inside the Academy unless they want something badly.
Selena has not heard Guinevere laugh since the corridor.
By evening it says VEXANA: MISSING, in the same type as a roster. Guinevere stands before it with two fingers at her collar.

facts.t: Vexana pictures it hanging in the Citadel, GUINEVERE and VEXANA in big letters, with someone one day unable to read them.

Rain turns its flower beds soft and black.
Below the bell tower its flower beds lie black and shining.
Selena rides in under its billboard.
Not long after the missing board went up, Vexana stepped out of the dark into Selena's lamp at the crews' yard.
All Selena said about her changed hair was "Nice hair."
Selena sells openly, because Vexana cannot tell on her without telling on herself, and she pays in places.

ties.t: They met at the crews' yard.

facts.t: Vexana waited in the dark for him to leave before she stepped into Selena's lamp.
Selena has never seen her maker, but never doubted there was one: somebody made the hum in her bones.

Her name and Vexana's are on the courtyard billboard in big letters.

At the breach she punched Enders out of the air.
On the stairs she laughs loudest at Selena, her head thrown back, with Vexana a few steps behind.

Selena has not heard her laugh since the corridor.
